capture.$measureFrames: 1800 rather than 900 so the measured window is 30 simulated seconds at dt 1/60. At 900 the walking routes covered 67 m — half a chunk — and a streaming system that never crossed a chunk boundary would have measured as free. Raising a measurement window makes the gate stricter, never weaker.
capture.$estimator: THE MEDIAN OF THREE RUNS' p95, AND THE CEILING DID NOT MOVE. CONTRACT §0 rule 6. Session 4b closed with `downtown_dense` wall p95 landing at 11.20 / 11.40 / 11.70 / 12.20 / 12.60 ms across five observations against a 12.5 ms ceiling, and the gate went red about one run in three. THE BREACH IS 12.60 - 12.50 = 0.10 ms. THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN RUN-TO-RUN RESOLUTION, MEASURED ON A QUIET MACHINE IN THE SAME SESSION, IS 0.40 TO 0.80 ms. The breach is 0.10/0.40 = 25% to 0.10/0.80 = 12.5% of the noise floor, so a single run compared against a fixed ceiling was deciding on a difference the instrument cannot resolve. The pooled median is 11.70 ms, clear by 0.80 ms. WHAT CHANGED IS THE ESTIMATOR AND NOT THE BOUND: `wallFrameMsP95` is still 12.5.
capture.$estimator_whyMedian: MEDIAN OF PER-RUN p95, NOT THE MEAN AND NOT p95 OVER POOLED FRAMES. Against the mean: with sigma = 0.55 ms taken from the observed spread, a single draw has a standard error of 0.55 ms, the mean of three has 0.55/sqrt(3) = 0.32 ms and the median of three normal draws has variance 0.449*sigma^2, so 0.670*0.55 = 0.37 ms. The mean is 16% tighter and it carries a drifted run at full weight, and drift on this machine is ONE-SIDED — session 4b's three baseline runs rose monotonically on all six series as the load average went 2.62 to 2.95. A median of three discards exactly one contaminated observation, which is the contamination pattern actually observed. 16% of efficiency is the price of that and it is worth paying. Against p95 over pooled frames: THAT IS A DIFFERENT QUANTITY. `wallFrameMsP95` was derived against a single run's p95; the p95 of frames pooled from three runs is the 95th percentile of a MIXTURE, whose value depends on how far the runs drifted apart and whose upper tail is filled preferentially by whichever run caught the load spike. Comparing it to a ceiling written for the per-run p95 is CONTRACT §9's shape exactly — a number computed correctly and then used as though it were a different quantity, with the same units and a plausible magnitude. The median of per-run p95s changes the number of draws and nothing else.
capture.$estimator_notALoosening: WHAT THIS IS NOT ALLOWED TO BE, and the self-test that holds it to that. A pooled estimator is a way to make a gate quieter, and quieter is one step from unfailable — CONTRACT §0 rule 5 violated by an estimator rather than by a number. So `perfcheck --falsify` carries FOUR estimator cases, two of which must reject: 11.20/11.40/12.60 must be green (one drifted run is the case this change exists for), 12.60/12.70/12.80 must be red (three runs over is a regression), 11.20/12.60/12.70 must be red (the median tolerates ONE contaminated observation and no more, which is the boundary of the claim), and 12.50/12.50/12.50 must be green (the comparison was always strictly greater-than). COUNTS ARE NOT MEDIANED: §9 rule 6's corollary is that counts do not drift, so each count bound gets the run that is worst FOR IT — the maximum for a ceiling, the minimum for a floor — which is strictly stricter than the single run this replaced.
capture.$runs: 3. Two would make the median the mean of the middle pair, which is the mean with extra steps and no robustness. motionVectors.$comment: CONTRACT §5.12. Per-instance motion vectors: a second instanced attribute holding the previous frame's instanceMatrix, double-buffered and swapped. Two numbers live here because both are decisions rather than measurements, and both were taken BEFORE the vehicle renderer was written rather than discovered at pedestrian scale.
motionVectors.$derivation_minExtentPx: THE SIZE BELOW WHICH AN INSTANCE GETS NO MOTION VECTOR AT ALL, AND IT COMES FROM THE CLAMP RATHER THAN FROM TASTE. A motion vector exists to stop the TAA neighbourhood clamp rejecting an object's own history every frame (§5.11: it aliases rather than ghosts). The clamp can only reject displaced history when the clip box EXCLUDES the background — and the box is built from a 3x3 neighbourhood of the current frame (src/modules/post.js, the y,x loop over [-1,1]). So a fragment can only express reprojection error if its entire 3x3 neighbourhood lies inside the object's silhouette. Under TAA jitter the silhouette's sub-pixel phase is arbitrary: the jitter is Halton(2,3) minus 0.5, so plus or minus half a pixel (src/modules/post.js, JITTER). A 1-D interval of length w at arbitrary phase covers AT LEAST floor(w) - 1 pixels completely, so three consecutive fully-covered pixels require floor(w) - 1 >= 3, i.e. w >= 4. BOTH screen dimensions must satisfy it, so the binding quantity is the instance's SMALLEST projected extent, not its bounding sphere. 4 px is therefore a property of a 3x3 filter under half-pixel jitter and is independent of resolution and field of view, in exactly the way `particles.maxStreakLengthPx` = 56 is a property of a raindrop.
motionVectors.$derivation_crosscheck: THE SAME NUMBER, REACHED FROM THE OTHER END. `particles.maxStreakWidthPx` is 3 — a 1 px core plus a half-pixel soft edge each side, derived from what an antialiased line needs under TAA jitter and written a session before this threshold existed. 3 < 4, so a rain streak can NEVER qualify for a motion vector. Rain being excluded is therefore an arithmetic consequence of two independent derivations agreeing, and not a special case somebody remembered to write. CONTRACT §9 rule 2.
motionVectors.$kindMinExtentM: The smallest OVERALL BODY dimension of each moving kind, in metres. Cutoff distance is minExtentM / (minExtentPx * theta) where theta = 2*tan(fovY/2)/internalHeight is one pixel in radians, computed per frame from the live projection rather than baked: at the gate's 50 deg vertical fov and 1440 internal lines theta = 6.4765e-4 rad, so 4 px = 2.5906e-3 rad and the cutoffs are wedge 1.42 m -> 548.1 m, pod 1.66 m -> 640.8 m, van 2.16 m -> 833.8 m, hauler 2.66 m -> 1026.8 m, moto 0.63 m -> 243.2 m, pedestrian 0.45 m -> 173.7 m. particles.$comment: Additive billboard layers — rain streaks, splash, spray. A PAIR of bounds, because a count cap alone is not a fill bound: 700 unbounded additive billboards are 700 LARGE billboards the moment one drifts past the lens. The count is read off the live scene (`instanceMatrix.count`), the area is a compile-time clamp in the vertex shader, and their product is a fill that is bounded by construction rather than by hope.
particles.$derivation_count: MARSHALL–PALMER. N(D) = N0·exp(−Λ·D) with N0 = 8000 m^-3 mm^-1 and Λ = 4.1·R^-0.21 mm^-1. At the night_rain route's R = 10 mm/h: Λ = 4.1 × 10^-0.21 = 4.1 × 0.6166 = 2.528 mm^-1, so the number density over all diameters is n = N0/Λ = 8000/2.528 = 3164 drops per m^3 and the median-volume diameter is D0 = 3.67/Λ = 1.452 mm. THE COUNT IS NOT ALL OF THEM AND CANNOT BE: 3164 per m^3 over any volume worth drawing is millions. What Marshall–Palmer supplies is not the count but WHERE THE SPLIT IS between a drop that is a streak and a drop that is a veil, and that is a number this project can check. Simulated volume: the frustum wedge out to the street's own half-width, because past the kerb-to-kerb width the streaks inside one pixel overlap and the correct model is the participating medium this project already renders (ATM.hazeDensity), not more billboards. CORRIDOR is 11.7 m, so take 12 m; the 50° vertical fov at 16:9 gives a solid angle of 4·asin(sin 39.6° · sin 25°) = 1.094 sr, so V = Ω·d³/3 = 1.094 × 1728 / 3 = 630 m^3. 700 instances in 630 m^3 is 1.11 drops per m^3, which Marshall–Palmer reaches at D ≥ 3.15 mm: 3164 · e^(−2.528 × 3.15) = 3164 × 3.51e-4 = 1.11. By mass that is Γ(4, 7.96)/Γ(4) = 4.4% of the rainfall and by number 0.035% of it. SO THE CAP IS A STATEMENT AND IT IS FALSIFIABLE: everything below 3.15 mm is not missing, it is the veil — and if 4b renders drops smaller than that as billboards it is double-counting water the haze term is already delivering.
particles.$derivation_area: THE CLAMP, AND WHY IT IS A MAXIMUM AND NOT A MINIMUM. One pixel at the internal resolution (2560×1440, CONTRACT §5.10) at 50° vertical fov is θ = 2·tan(25°)/1440 = 6.48e-4 rad. A drop of diameter D0 = 1.452 mm is one pixel WIDE at d = D0/θ = 2.24 m. Its terminal velocity is v = 3.78·D0^0.67 = 3.78 × 1.288 = 4.87 m/s (Atlas–Ulbrich), so at dt = 1/60 s its motion-blurred streak is ℓ = 81.2 mm long and is one pixel LONG out to ℓ/θ = 125 m. A rain streak is therefore a sub-pixel-wide line everywhere except the nearest two metres, which is the whole reason rain is a screen-space effect — and the reason the clamp has to bound the near field, where the same drop becomes a billboard. maxStreakLengthPx falls straight out of those two: at the distance where the streak first fills a pixel in width it is ℓ/D0 = 81.2/1.452 = 55.9 px long. THAT RATIO IS THE STREAK'S OWN ASPECT AND IS INDEPENDENT OF RESOLUTION AND FOV — a raindrop cannot be longer than 56× its own width without being something other than a raindrop, which is what makes 56 a bound rather than a taste. maxStreakWidthPx is 3: a 1-px core plus a half-pixel soft edge each side, the narrowest quad that can carry an antialiased line under TAA jitter.
particles.$derivation_fill: 700 × (3 × 56) = 117 600 px of additive overdraw against 2560 × 1440 = 3 686 400, which is 3.19%. maxFillFraction is 0.035 — just above the delivered figure, which is what a ceiling is for. THE ASSERTION IS ON THE PRODUCT AND NOT ON EITHER TERM: `perfcheck` reads maxInstances off the live scene and maxAreaPx off the shader's own #defines, multiplies them, and fails if the product exceeds the fill. Either number alone can be met while the fill is unbounded.
particles.$derivation_split: THREE LAYERS OUT OF ONE CAP, AND THE SPLIT IS NOT ARBITRARY BECAUSE TWO OF THEM MUST BE DRAWING THE SAME WATER. 4a's 700 was derived as one number for one layer. Splitting it across streaks, splash and spray needs a rule, and the rule is that the streak layer and the splash layer are the AIR and the GROUND views of a single drop population: if the diameter threshold implied by the streak count and the one implied by the splash count disagree, one layer is depicting water the other says is not there. Solve them together. SPRAY IS FIRST because it is attached to vehicles rather than to the rainfall: 6 vehicles in the near field x 2 wheel lines x 6 puffs = 72, taken as 70. That leaves 630 for a SHARED threshold D. Streaks: n(>=D) * V with V = 629.2 m^3 (4a's frustum wedge, reproduced here to 0.1 m^3 by independent integration). Splash: flux(>=D) * A * L, where flux(>=D) = integral of N0*exp(-Lambda*D')*v(D') dD' over D' >= D, A is the road-plus-pavement area inside the frustum out to 15 m, and L is the crown lifetime. A: the horizontal fov is 79.32 deg, so the frustum reaches the 23.4 m corridor at 14.11 m, giving A = tan(39.66 deg)*14.11^2 + 23.4*(15 - 14.11) = 164.8 + 20.8 = 185.9 m^2, taken as 186. WHY 15 m: a crown is about 3 drop diameters across, so 3 x 3.28 mm = 9.8 mm, which is one pixel at 9.8e-3 / 6.4765e-4 = 15.1 m. L = 0.10 s, six frames at 60 Hz, which is the low end of a measured splash crown's 50-100 ms rise and collapse. Solving n(>=D)*629.2 + flux(>=D)*18.6 = 630 gives D = 3.281 mm, streaks 497.2, splash 132.8. Rounded to 500 and 130, and inverting each independently gives D >= 3.279 mm from the streaks and D >= 3.290 mm from the splash — the two agree to 0.011 mm, which is the coherence check the split exists to pass. THE CLAIM: this session draws the largest 3.47% of the rainfall BY MASS and 0.0250% of it BY NUMBER, and everything below 3.28 mm is the veil `setHaze` delivers. Falsifiable in the same way 4a's was.
particles.$derivation_split_units: A UNIT DISCREPANCY THAT IS REAL AND IS NOT A DEFECT, WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE §9 RULE 4 SAYS TO PRINT BOTH. Integrating this same distribution against the Atlas-Ulbrich fall speed reconstructs a rainfall rate of 11.08 mm/h, not the nominal 10.00 the Lambda(R) relation was evaluated at. The 10.8% gap is between two published fits — Marshall-Palmer's Lambda = 4.1*R^-0.21 was derived against a different terminal-velocity law from 3.78*D^0.67 — and not an arithmetic error. Both numbers are here so the next session disagrees with the fits rather than with the code. Nothing in the split depends on which of the two is used: all three layer counts are ratios within one distribution.
particles.$requireLayers: ALL THREE, BY NAME, READ OFF THE LIVE SCENE. Without this the pair-bound is satisfied by shipping one layer, and a fill of 2.28% with two systems missing is a green that means nothing — the same shape as an empty scene satisfying every fill bound, one level up.
particles.$layerCaps: Per-layer instance ceiling and the compile-time screen-area clamp each layer's shader must declare. The gate reads the count off `instanceMatrix.count` and the area off the material's own `NOCTIS_PARTICLE_MAX_AREA_PX` define, never off the declaration. Areas: a streak is 3 x 56 = 168 (4a's derivation, unchanged); a splash crown is 8 x 8 = 64, being 9.8 mm at the 1-px distance of 15 m expanded by the 2.5x a collapsing crown's ring reaches, floor-projected and therefore square rather than elongated; a spray puff is 12 x 12 = 144, a 0.30 m turbulent ball at 1 px per 9.8 mm read at its own 25 m visibility limit and clamped where it passes the lens.
particles.$deliveredFill: 500*168 + 130*64 + 70*144 = 84000 + 8320 + 10080 = 102400 px against 2560*1440 = 3686400, which is 2.778%. The pair-bound's own worst case — all 700 instances at the 168 px clamp — is 3.190%, and the ceiling stays at 3.5%. The ceiling is NOT tightened to the delivered figure: `maxFillFraction` bounds what the PAIR permits, and the pair still permits 3.190%.
particles.$requireClampIsCompileTime: The screen-size clamp must be a #define in the vertex shader, not a uniform. A clamp that can change at runtime is a clamp nobody can budget — the same rule §5.8 applies to the SSR march's step count. perfcheck asserts the layer reports its clamp as compile-time.

trafficLights.$comment: Headlights, as a claim about the clustered grid rather than about vehicles. The binding limit is CLUSTER.maxPerCluster (96 since this session), NOT CLUSTER.maxLights (384): a light in the pool costs five texels of a data texture, a light in a froxel costs one iteration of the fragment loop for every pixel of that froxel. Those two numbers now live adjacent in src/core/constants.js for exactly that reason.
trafficLights.$derivation: FROXEL INDEX SATURATION. The grid is 16 × 9 × 24 = 3456 froxels. A light claims every froxel its bounding volume touches, and the cap that binds is per-froxel. The pool reservation is measured, not authored: the origin block allocates 52 lights and the streamed lamp pool 196, which is 248 before a vehicle exists, so 248 + 96 = 344 of 384 with 40 to spare. 96 = 48 vehicles × 2 headlights. BUT WHAT FIXES 48 IS THE FROXEL AND NOT THE POOL, and the pool is nowhere near binding — measured, the worst route has only 160 of 384 lights in view at once, because the lamp pool is a pool and only the lamps near the camera are lit.
trafficLights.$measured: SWEEP, night_rain, 600 frames per point, placeholder headlights at the cone bound, jammed four abreast nose-to-tail down the view axis (`node tools/clustercheck.mjs --sweep`). Vehicles → worst froxel of 96: 0 → 34, 12 → 34, 24 → 43, 36 → 53, 48 → 65, 60 → 73, 72 → 77, 96 → 80. The curve is concave — the froxels traffic fills are the ones traffic has already filled — so the cap is not where the grid runs out but where the margin stops being worth having: 48 vehicles leaves 31, and 96 vehicles would leave 16 for twice the content. THE OLD CAP OF 48 PER FROXEL COULD NOT HAVE HELD ANY OF IT: 65 at 48 vehicles overflows 48 by 17, and even 24 vehicles at 43 leaves 5.
trafficLights.$measured_full: FULL ROUTES, 1800 frames, 48 vehicles / 96 headlights, cone bound on. downtown_dense: worst froxel 66 of 96, margin 30, 0 froxels at cap, pool 160 of 384. highway_speed: 62 of 96, margin 34, pool 116 of 384. night_rain: 75 of 96, margin 21, pool 160 of 384. No overflow on any route. THE MARGIN IS 21, on night_rain, and that is the number 4b starts from.
trafficLights.$derivation_cone: THE CONE BOUND. Until this session every light was bounded by a sphere of `radius` centred on the light — exact for a point light, wildly conservative for a beam. A spot's support is a spherical SECTOR, and the sphere circumscribing a sector of range R and half-angle θ has radius R/(2·cos θ) centred R/(2·cos θ) along the axis. The VOLUME ratio is 1/(8·cos³θ), which at the headlight bound θ = 35° (a 70° beam) is 1/(8 × 0.81915³) = 1/(8 × 0.54952) = 1/4.396 → 4.40× less frustum claimed. It is a win below θ = 60° and a loss above it, because at 60° exactly R/(2·cos 60°) = R and the two spheres coincide; that crossover is CLUSTER.coneBoundMaxHalfAngle and it is geometry, not tuning.
trafficLights.$measured_cone: 4.40× IS THE VOLUME RATIO AND IT IS NOT THE FROXEL-WRITE RATIO. Measured, night_rain, 600 frames, `node tools/clustercheck.mjs --route=night_rain --frames=600 --vehicles=N`: at N = 0 the bounded and unbounded runs write 23 202 indices each — EXACTLY equal, because every spot light in the world today is a street lantern whose outer cone is LUMINAIRE.alongRoadRad = 68°, above the 60° crossover, so the bound is a no-op on all of them and the whole saving is the headlights'. At N = 12 (24 headlights) the pair is 55 269 bounded against 83 106 unbounded. Subtracting the common baseline isolates the headlights exactly: 32 067 bounded against 59 904 unbounded, which is 1336 and 2496 froxel writes per headlight and a ratio of 1.87×. NOT 4.40×, and the gap is a quantity confusion of exactly the CONTRACT §9 shape — a volume ratio read as a froxel-write ratio. Froxel writes are not proportional to volume for three reasons, all of them structural: assignment bounds a SPHERE by its screen-space AABB, which is 6/π = 1.91× the sphere's own area before anything else; the AABB is then quantised UP to whole tiles, which dominates for anything spanning a couple of tiles; and both are clamped to the screen, so an oversized sphere's excess is clipped away and never counted at all — 16 × 9 tiles is the most any light can claim however large it is. The 4.40× is right about the frustum and the 1.87× is right about the cost, and the second is the one that was worth measuring. At N = 48 the unbounded run drives the flat index list to CLUSTER.maxIndices = 131 072 exactly on all three routes and the assignment loop breaks early, so the ratio there is a lower bound and not a measurement; that is why the isolation is run at 12.
trafficLights.$vehicles_IS_THE_PROBE_NOT_THE_CONTENT: SESSION 4b SPLITS A WORD THAT WAS DOING TWO JOBS. `vehicles` is the PLACEHOLDER PROBE's vehicle count and nothing else: `harness.saturateTraffic` makes two headlights per vehicle (harness.js), so 48 here is what produces the 96 lights the froxel measurement was made with, and `tools/clustercheck.mjs` reads this field as its default. The SHIPPED content is 96 vehicles with ONE clustered headlamp each — see `content` below. The light count is the quantity both agree on and it is 96 either way, which is why the 4a measurement transfers; the vehicle count is not, and calling both of them `vehicles` is how a number starts meaning two things. Left at 48 deliberately rather than renamed, because renaming it would change what clustercheck measures on a field whose whole value is that it reproduces a previous run.
trafficLights.$content: WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPS, AND WHY IT IS NOT WORSE FOR THE GRID THAN THE PROBE. 160 vehicles and 96 headlamps, the pool assigned each frame to the nearest 96. THE VEHICLE COUNT AND THE LIGHT COUNT ARE TWO BUDGETS: 96 vehicles was the first version and it put one vehicle every 18.4 m, which is a real arterial flow and reads as a quiet night (measured from a plan view of the block street: three vehicles in fifty metres). city.js already separates these two for its street lamps, and the same argument is stronger here -- a headlamp is worth its road pool, that pool is invisible past a hundred metres, and what makes a distant vehicle read is its emissive light LINE, which costs no slot. 160 vehicles at one every 11.07 m is 975 veh/h/lane against a saturation flow near 1800, and the 96 lit ones fill the nearest 147 m. The probe put 96 lights in PAIRS 1.5 m apart on 48 vehicles jammed at a 7 m headway from 8 m in front of the lens — the densest arrangement two lanes each way can produce, which is what makes it a bound. The content puts the same 96 lights SINGLY, one per vehicle, over 1771 m of centreline at an 18.4 m mean spacing. Same pool cost (96 of the 96 reserved), strictly lower froxel concentration, so the probe's margin of 21 on night_rain is a floor under the content's and not an estimate of it. Tail lights, brake lights, indicators and interior glow are EMISSIVE GEOMETRY AND CONSUME ZERO LIGHT SLOTS: a tail lamp is about 60 cd (0.5 lux at 11 m x 121 m^2), which against a carriageway held at LIGHT.streetAverageLux = 16 lux contributes 3% of the ambient at the distance it is seen from and nothing at all beyond it — it is not illumination, it is a thing the SSR puts in the wet road for free.
trafficLights.$derivation_contentCount: WHERE 96 VEHICLES COMES FROM, WHICH IS A FLOW RATE AND NOT A TASTE. Roads run along every chunk boundary at a 128 m pitch in both directions, so the road-length density is 2/128 = 0.015625 m of centreline per m^2 of ground, and the centreline length inside a disc of radius R is 0.015625 * pi * R^2. At the simulated radius of 190 m that is 1771 m. 96 vehicles over 1771 m is one every 18.45 m across four lanes, i.e. 73.8 m per vehicle per lane, which at the 12 m/s free-flow speed is 3600 * 12 / 73.8 = 585 vehicles per hour per lane. That is an ordinary urban arterial at night — busy enough that the street is never empty, quiet enough that nothing queues except at a signal. 190 m is inside the 256 m minimum radius at which road SURFACE geometry exists (city.js draws the carriageway only for ring <= 2), so no vehicle is ever driving on the global ground plane.
trafficLights.$contentLightsPerVehicle: At most one, and only for the nearest 96. Asserted as countByRole(traffic) == contentHeadlamps rather than <=: too FEW is the failure that says a headlamp pool silently stopped being created, and it is the one an inequality would hide.
trafficLights.$minBodyTypes: Silhouettes carry the setting. Four or five body types that read as 2049 rather than as now: proportions unlike current wheel-arch geometry, different roof heights, and light signatures that are LINES rather than lamps. Five, and the floor is at 4 so that losing one to a bug is a failure rather than a shrug. Roof heights delivered: 1.28 / 1.92 / 2.45 / 3.10 / 1.30 m — a 2.4x spread, which is what stops a queue reading as one repeated object.
trafficLights.$maxNonTrafficRoleLightsPerVehicle: Zero. Everything lit on a vehicle except the headlamp is emissive geometry with no slot.
trafficLights.$requireNoOverflow: `clusterOverflow` false on all three routes WITH THE POOL SATURATED. Saturated is the load-bearing word: with no traffic in the world the assertion is true of a grid holding 248 lights and says nothing about one holding 344, which is the grid 4b ships against. perfcheck fails it as unrun — not as passed — until harness.saturateTraffic() has made the lights.
trafficLights.$minOccupancyMargin: maxPerCluster minus the worst froxel over the whole run. A boolean cannot answer 'does traffic fit': `clusterOverflow: false` at 96 of 96 and at 31 of 96 are the same boolean and completely different findings.
trafficLights.$minOccupancyMargin_4b: RAISED from 8 to 40 against the delivered city. Measured worst froxel with the real traffic on: downtown_dense 39 of 96, highway_speed 11, night_rain 34, so margins of 57, 85 and 62. 4a's placeholder measured a margin of 21 at 48 vehicles x 2 headlights jammed nose to tail down the view axis with a 30 m throw and a 35 deg cone; the content is easier than the probe in three separate ways — the lights are singles rather than pairs, they are spread over 1771 m of centreline rather than a queue, and the throw is 20 m rather than 30 — and it measures easier by exactly the amount those predict. 40 is under the worst delivered 57 with room for the camera to find a denser junction than any route visits.
trafficLights.$minStopLineM: SESSION 21, AND THE INSTRUMENT HAS BEEN BUILT SINCE SESSION 19. `traffic.stats().worstStopLineM` is the distance from a HELD vehicle`s FRONT to its own stop line, worst over the run; positive is short of the line, which is where a vehicle should stop, and NEGATIVE IS A DEFECT. Session 19 measured four of the five body types stopping past it — wedge 1.20 m, van 1.50 m, hauler 3.30 m, i.e. 80% of a tractor unit into the kerbside crossing lane — because `toStop` subtracted the distance to the vehicle`s ORIGIN and used it as the distance to its NOSE (CONTRACT §9`s table, session 19). The repair shipped in the same session; the ASSERTION did not, and STATE 20 §7 carried it as five minutes of work for two sessions running. THE FLOOR IS 0.0 AND IT IS THE ONLY DEFENSIBLE NUMBER: the quantity is a signed clearance and its sign IS the verdict. `Infinity` — no vehicle held at a red anywhere on the route — is UNRUN and fails, because a stop-line check on a route where nobody stopped is CONTRACT §7.1`s quiet gate. IT IS ALSO NOW A CHECK ON THE PAINT: `city.js` draws the stop bar from the same `CITY.stopLineFromJunctionM` the braking constraint reads, so a vehicle whose front is short of its own line is a vehicle whose front is short of the line you can see.
trafficLights.$minStopLineM_MEASURED_RED: SESSION 21 MEASURED IT AND IT IS RED: worst clearance -10.62 m over 108 simulated seconds on `downtown_dense` (`tools/perf-out/queueprobe-downtown_dense.log`). That is NOT session 19's defect returning — the missing front overhang is repaired — it is the other half of the session-21 brief's own suspicion: VEHICLES QUEUE INTO THE JUNCTION BOX. Car-following stops a vehicle behind the one in front wherever that is, and nothing stops it entering a box whose exit is blocked. The same run measured the queues themselves: 15 junctions, worst single queue 5 vehicles, EVERY ONE reaching zero within the window and none trending upward — so the mechanism exists and the deadlock it predicts does not, at 160 vehicles. THE FLOOR IS NOT MOVED. A signed clearance whose sign is the verdict has one defensible floor and this is it; what the next session owes it is a re-measurement at dt = 1/60 on a machine that can finish one (this was taken at dt = 0.1, the top of CONTRACT §4.2's clamp, because SwiftShader could not), and then a repair that reserves the EXIT of the box rather than the box.

silhouettes.$comment: WHAT A VEHICLE LOOKS LIKE, MEASURED OFF THE DELIVERED FRAME. CONTRACT §7.1, second rule. `trafficLights.minBodyTypes` counts kinds; it passed at 5 while all five kinds were flat-topped boxes with no wheel line, no glazing and no dark gap at the ground, and it could not have failed, because a floor that counts categories cannot see that every category is the same shape. This block is the paired assertion that measures the property the count was assumed to carry.
silhouettes.$mechanism: `harness.silhouettes()` projects the corners of every body box of every visible vehicle and pedestrian into SCREENSHOT PIXELS and returns nothing else — no colour, no luminance, no verdict. `tools/lib/silhouette.mjs` rasterises the union of the per-box convex hulls against `page.screenshot()` and every number below comes out of those pixels. The obvious alternative is a mask render pass and CONTRACT §8 forbids it for the reason it forbids `showMotion`: a gate that renders its own subject has stopped measuring the frame that ships.
silhouettes.$routes: DAYLIGHT ONLY, AND THE RESTRICTION IS THE CLAIM RATHER THAN A CONVENIENCE. What is being asserted is that a vehicle is identifiable as a vehicle when the sun is the light source. At midnight a vehicle is identifiable by its emissive light lines — which work, which is why night_rain and downtown_dense are the frames this project is proud of — and running the same metric there would measure the street lighting and the tail lamps rather than the body. `highway_speed` is the one route at t = 0.5. The list is asserted to be non-empty AND to be a subset of capture.routes, so renaming a route makes this loud rather than quiet: an assertion that silently applies to no route is the exact failure mode §7.1 exists for.
silhouettes.$estimator: THE SUBJECTS ARE POOLED ACROSS RUNS AND THE COUNT FLOORS ARE NOT. CONTRACT §0 rule 6, applied to a population rather than to a frame time, added in session 10. The poses used to be captured on the LAST run only, with a comment recording that the population is not identical between runs (`--runs=1` reported 19 vehicles and 57 pedestrians measurable, `--runs=3` reported 17 and 55, with the vehicle ground contrast moving 0.6561 to 0.7293 and its pass fraction ACROSS the 0.75 floor). Three poses is a sample of about fourteen vehicles, and a pass fraction over fourteen carries a standard error near 12 points against a floor 4 points away — which is how `highway_speed` reported a tone profile of 10/14 = 71% against 75%, and a width population of 4 against 5, for five consecutive sessions on content nobody had changed. NOW: every run captures the poses, and `summariseSilhouettes` measures the union. A MEDIAN or a PASS FRACTION is an estimate of a population property, so nine poses estimate the same quantity as three with 1/sqrt(3) of the error and no threshold moves. A COUNT FLOOR (`minMeasured`, `minProfileMeasured`, `minWidthMeasured`) asks whether ONE run saw enough subjects to say anything, so it takes the MEDIAN OF THE PER-RUN COUNTS instead — pooling those would multiply them by the number of runs and satisfy `minWidthMeasured: 5` with arithmetic rather than with the route, which is rule 5 broken by an estimator. NOT A LOOSENING, AND `perfcheck --falsify` HOLDS IT TO THAT: the count-floor cases still reject a fixture whose counts sit under the floor, and the fraction cases still reject a fixture whose fraction sits under `minPassFraction`. The cost is 6 extra pose captures on the one route in `routes`.
silhouettes.$poses: POOLED OVER THREE POSITIONS ON THE ROUTE, AND THAT IS THE SAME CORRECTION THIS SESSION MAKES TO THE FRAME-TIME ESTIMATOR. The end of a route is ONE camera position: measured at 1800 frames `highway_speed` finishes with 27 vehicles inside 60 m, and at 600 frames it finishes with 14. Neither is noise — the route is deterministic and both figures reproduce — but both are samples of one, and a content floor read off a sample of one is a claim about wherever the path happened to stop. Three parameters along the SAME route triples the population. NOT `setShotAt`: CONTRACT §8 forbids a gate rendering through an operator-chosen placement, and these come from the route's own spline at a parameter, which is the call `runRoute` already makes on every one of its 1800 frames. Taken AFTER the probe's report, so nothing here is inside the measured window.
silhouettes.$poses_notEndpoint: AND NOT 1.0. Measured: `camera.setRouteAt(name, 1)` points the eye at the sky, because the look-ahead that gives the camera its target runs off the end of the spline and the fallback direction is up. A pose there reports zero subjects within 60 m and every floor below fails as unrun — correctly, and for a reason that has nothing to do with vehicles. The three parameters are inside the path on both ends. The route's own last frame is unaffected: `runRoute` covers `speed * dt * frames / pathLength`, which on all three routes is under 1.
silhouettes.$poseFrames: 24 frames at each pose. TAA.settleFrames is what a look capture uses to converge the history; 24 is above it, and the history is dropped at the pose so the frame being measured is not a blend of two camera positions.
silhouettes.$maxDistanceM: 60 m, AND IT IS THE 4 px OF §5.12 REACHED FROM A THIRD DIRECTION. One pixel at the gate viewport is theta = 2*tan(25 deg)/1440 = 6.4765e-4 rad. The smallest feature this block asserts on is the ground gap under a body, which on a car is a 0.16 m clearance; for that to span 4 px the vehicle must be nearer than 0.16 / (4 * 6.4765e-4) = 61.76 m. Rounded DOWN to 60. Beyond it the metric would be measuring the resampler rather than the vehicle, and `motionVectors.minExtentPx` already derived the same 4 px from the TAA neighbourhood clamp under half-pixel jitter. Two independent derivations, one number.
silhouettes.$minAreaPx: PER KIND, because the two kinds have different aspect ratios and the binding constraint is rows rather than area. VEHICLE 1200 px^2: the ground band is 12% of the silhouette height, so the subject needs enough rows for that band to be more than a sampling accident, and 1200 px^2 at a car's 3.8:1 side aspect is 67 x 18 px whose bottom 12% is 2 rows and 134 samples. PEDESTRIAN 600 px^2: a person is 1.72 m tall and 0.595 m across the arms, so at maxDistanceM the mask is 41 x 14 px before the gaps between the limbs are subtracted, and the width profile needs 41 rows of at least minRowSamples each, which is 246 px. 600 is above that with margin and below what a 40 m figure delivers (66 x 23 x 0.55 fill = 835 px^2). Below this the subject is dropped rather than measured, and `minMeasured` is what stops dropping everything from reading as a pass.
silhouettes.$minMeasured: PER KIND, AND IT IS THE UNRUN GUARD. Zero measured subjects satisfies every floor below trivially — the same shape as an empty particle layer satisfying every fill bound (CONTRACT §10 step 3). VEHICLE 6, PEDESTRIAN 8, both against three pooled poses. THE ARITHMETIC for the pedestrian figure: 360 pedestrians over the 3x3 chunk ring of 128 m chunks is 360 / 147 456 m^2 = 2.44e-3 per m^2, and the forward half-disc out to the 40 m where a figure still clears minAreaPx is pi*40^2/2 = 2513 m^2, giving 6.1 expected per pose and 18 over three. 8 is well under that and above what occlusion between people walking in groups can take away. For vehicles the same disc on 160 vehicles confined to the carriageway delivered 27 eligible in one measured pose; 6 over three poses is a floor a broken minority cannot reach.
silhouettes.$groundBandFraction: 0.12. The bottom eighth of the silhouette's own height, which for the 1.28 m wedge is 0.154 m — the ground clearance itself, 0.16 m, to within the quantisation. A fraction of the SILHOUETTE and not of the frame, so the same vehicle at 10 m and at 40 m measures the same thing and the number is not a proxy for distance.
silhouettes.$bodyBand: The 30–70% band of the silhouette height, which is the body side on every one of the five types. It is the reference the ground band is divided by. SESSION 8 CORRECTION TO A CLAIM THAT WAS ALREADY FALSE WHEN 7c SHIPPED: 'contains no glazing on any of them' held for four types, not five — the hauler's cab screen sat at 0.57-0.65 of its height in 7c and sits at 0.49-0.56 now, inside the band both times. The band's job survives it: a dark stripe in the reference band darkens the body-side mean slightly, which moves ground contrast in the STRICT direction, and the delivered margin (1.5x+ the 0.45 floor) carries it.
silhouettes.$minGroundContrast: 0.45, i.e. the ground band must read at most 0.55x the body band. THE PHYSICS, so the next session can disagree with the model rather than the taste. The underside of a vehicle sees the sky through two long slots. For an infinite slot of half-width 0.975 m (a 1.95 m body) under a 0.16 m clearance, the sky is visible from the centre of the floor only between the horizon and alpha = atan(0.16/0.975) = 9.3216 deg on each side, and the cosine-weighted fraction of the hemisphere in those two wedges is 1 - cos(alpha) = 0.013194. One bounce off a road of albedo 0.15 and an underside of 0.05 gives an effective 0.013194 / (1 - 0.12*0.986806) = 0.014966, so the underbody receives 1.4966% of the open road's illuminance. The body SIDE is a vertical surface seeing about half the sky plus, at noon, the sun; taken conservatively at 40% of the open road, the radiance ratio is 0.014966/0.40 = 0.0374 and the contrast is 0.9626. THE FLOOR IS 0.45, WHICH IS 14.7x LOOSER THAN THE PHYSICS, and it is loose on purpose: the measurement is made after ACES and after the §5.5 veiling glare, both of which compress the ratio toward 1 (the conservative direction, making the floor harder to pass, not easier), and the bottom row of the mask is antialiased against the road.
silhouettes.$minGroundContrast_measured: WHAT A FLAT-BOTTOMED SLAB ACTUALLY SCORES, because the first draft of the sentence above said 'a slab scores 0 by construction' and that is not true. MEASURED on the boxes this session inherited: 0.235 median. It is not 0 because the §5.7 indirect field gives a wall less sky visibility near the pavement than at its top, so the bottom of a flat side is genuinely darker than its middle. 0.45 is therefore 1.91x the number a slab delivers rather than infinitely above it, and that ratio is the margin the assertion actually has. Written down because a floor whose stated headroom is wrong is a floor nobody can argue with.
silhouettes.$DISCARDED_darkFraction: A METRIC THAT WAS WRITTEN, MEASURED AND THROWN AWAY. Recorded so it is not written again. The first structure metric was the share of the silhouette below 45% of its own 90th percentile, on the reasoning that glazing and a wheel recess are far darker than paint. MEASURED ON THE FLAT BOXES IT EXISTED TO REJECT: 0.646 against a floor of 0.16 — four times green, on exactly the content that prompted the assertion. A convex solid in sunlight has one face lit and two not, so two thirds of its pixels sit below any threshold anchored to its brightest, and the metric was measuring WHICH FACE CAUGHT THE SUN. It would have shipped green and unfailable, which is the same defect as minBodyTypes one level down. This is the fifth time a check in this project has been able to answer only a question nobody was asking; it is the first time one was caught before it shipped, and the thing that caught it was CONTRACT §7.1's requirement to confirm the assertion RED against the current content before building anything.
silhouettes.$minLumaRoughness: 0.30. TOTAL VARIATION OVER RANGE, MINUS ONE, on the row-median luminance profile down the silhouette. A MONOTONE PROFILE SCORES EXACTLY ZERO whatever its contrast, which is what a flat-sided box produces down every column — with or without a sunlit top face, and with or without the §5.7 gradient that makes the bottom of a wall darker than its top. Only a profile that DOUBLES BACK scores above zero, and doubling back is what one material on flat faces cannot do. THE ARITHMETIC for a body with a roof, a glazing band, a painted side and a wheel recess: take the roof at 1.0 (sun plus sky on a horizontal face), the side at 0.60 (vertical, about half the sky plus a grazing sun), the glazing at reflectance 0.025 against paint at 0.08 plus a sky reflection at roughness 0.10, so 0.25, and the wheel recess at the 0.037 of body the ground-contact arithmetic above derives, so 0.022. TV = (1.00-0.25) + (0.60-0.25) + (0.60-0.022) = 1.678 and range = 1.00-0.022 = 0.978, giving 1.716 - 1 = 0.716. The floor is 0.30, which is 2.4x under the prediction, because the bands are only a few pixels tall at the far end of maxDistanceM and the profile is smoothed over max(3, rows/24) rows before the variation is taken.
silhouettes.$minWidthRoughness: 0.35, THE SAME STATISTIC ON THE SHAPE, and it is the pedestrian assertion. A person has no ground clearance and no glazing; what separates one from a bollard at street scale is an outline — a narrow head over wide shoulders over two legs with a gap between them. THE ARITHMETIC: head 0.17 m, shoulder span 0.595 m across the arms, two 0.145 m legs covering 0.29 m. The row-width profile runs 0.17 -> 0.595 -> 0.29, so TV = 0.425 + 0.305 = 0.730 against a range of 0.595 - 0.17 = 0.425, giving 1.718 - 1 = 0.718. The floor is 0.35, 2.05x under. A rectangle scores 0. Measured off the delivered frame and not off the body-type table: the mask is the union of the per-part convex hulls, so what is counted per row is how many pixels of the person are actually there.
silhouettes.$ROOFLINE: THE SILHOUETTE HEIGHT PROFILE, CONTRACT §7.3, AND IT IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE GEOMETRY IT ASKS FOR EXISTS. The three metrics above measure the ground gap, the tone down the body and the paint, and every one of them passes comfortably on a rectangular prism that is well coloured and stands on wheels — which is exactly what the fleet is: fifteen vehicles in `perf-out/highway_speed-u0_85.png` with a flat top, vertical sides and sharp corners in every direction. A floor that counts body types could not see it (that is §7.2, and it is why this block's siblings exist); neither can any of this block's siblings, because none of them looks at the OUTLINE along the vehicle's length. THE READING: at each of `stations` positions along the subject's own long axis the harness returns the projected image segment from the bottom of the subject to `overshoot` times its own height on its longitudinal mid-plane, and the gate reports how far up that segment the mask reaches. A rectangular prism reads THE SAME FRACTION AT EVERY STATION from any distance, any heading and any sun angle, so `roofSpan` is exactly 0.000 for one — the assertion fails on a box by construction rather than by calibration, which is the property `$DISCARDED_darkFraction` did not have.
silhouettes.$stations: 12 STATIONS, AND THE NUMBER COMES FROM THE NARROWEST FEATURE THE BLOCK CLAIMS TO SEE. A level has to occupy `minPlateauFraction` = 0.15 of the length to be a level rather than a notch, and 0.15 x 12 = 1.8, so the shallowest claim the sampling can support is 2 stations of 12. Fewer stations and a bonnet under a fifth of the length is one sample; more stations and each band is narrower than the 0.15 m gap between a hauler's cab and its trailer, which is real geometry and is not a change of level.
silhouettes.$subSamples: 3 PER STATION, AND THE GATE TAKES THEIR MAXIMUM, so a station reports the upper envelope of the roofline over its band rather than a point sample of it. THE ARITHMETIC: the band is length/12, which is 0.41 m on the 4.90 m wedge and 0.77 m on the 9.20 m hauler, so three sub-samples land every 0.14 m and 0.26 m respectively. The hauler's cab and trailer are separated by a 0.15 m gap in which the tallest thing is the sill at 0.66 m of a 3.22 m vehicle; a point sample that landed in it would report a height change of two thirds of the vehicle from 0.15 m of air, which is a sampling accident wearing the costume of a finding. With three sub-samples at most one can be in the gap and the maximum discards it.
silhouettes.$trim: 0.10 OF THE LENGTH OFF EACH END. The outermost tenth of a vehicle's own extent is bumper, wheel and the antialiased edge of one: the wedge's extent is +/-2.45 m and its wheels are at +/-1.55 m with a 0.62 m diameter, so the outer 0.49 m at each end is overhang. A roofline that included them would report the top of a tyre as a level, and the tyre is what the ground-contact assertion above already measures.
silhouettes.$overshoot: 1.15. The station segment has to reach ABOVE the highest geometry on the mid-plane, because the top edge of the silhouette at a station is the NEAR-SIDE top edge and that projects higher than the mid-plane point at the same world height. THE BOUND: for a half-width w at distance d the near edge subtends d/(d - w), which for w = 0.98 m (a 1.95 m body) at the population's nearest 12 m is 1.089. 1.15 covers it with margin; a segment that stopped at 1.00 would clip every near subject to exactly 1.000 at every station and report a prism's span for a shaped body.
silhouettes.$minStationPx: 4 PIXELS PER STATION OF PROJECTED LONG AXIS, so 48 px of axis for the 12 stations, AND IT IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT ARRIVAL OF THE SAME NUMBER. §5.12's `motionVectors.minExtentPx` derived 4 px from the TAA 3x3 neighbourhood clamp under half-pixel jitter; `maxDistanceM` above derived 60 m from the 0.16 m ground gap spanning 4 px at the gate's angular resolution; this derives it from the sampling grid, because two stations whose bands are under 4 px apart cannot be told apart after the antialiased edge of the mask is subtracted. A vehicle seen end-on — which on a route where the camera drives WITH the traffic is the vehicle directly ahead in the same lane — has its whole length inside a few columns, and a roofline squeezed into them is a measurement of the resampler. Excluded from the profile population on geometry alone, before a pixel is read.
silhouettes.$minStationFraction: 0.75 OF THE STATIONS MUST BE READABLE or the subject is dropped from the profile population. A station whose topmost own-mask pixel is claimed by a NEARER subject is dropped rather than read low, because a dropped station cannot manufacture a height change and a station read low can — the exclusion is in the direction that makes the assertion harder to pass, which is the same direction `minVisibleFraction`'s band check chose for the same reason. THE ARITHMETIC for 0.75: the two features the assertion is about are a low plateau and a high one, each at least `minPlateauFraction` = 0.15 of the length, so 0.30 of the length must survive plus the transition between them; a quarter of the length missing leaves room for both wherever it falls. `minProfileMeasured` per kind is what stops this emptying the population quietly.
silhouettes.$levelTolerance: 0.10 OF THE SUBJECT'S OWN HEIGHT — the height difference below which two stations are at the same level. THE ARITHMETIC, and it is the 4 px again: at `maxDistanceM` = 60 m a 1.42 m wedge is 1.42 / (60 x 6.4765e-4) = 36.55 px tall, and 4 px of that is 0.109. Two heights closer than that are not separable at the far end of the population that the block admits, so calling them separate levels would be reporting the resampler. Rounded down to 0.10.
silhouettes.$minPlateauFraction: 0.15 of the surviving stations before a cluster of station heights counts as a LEVEL rather than as a notch. A reference-era three-box body is bonnet, cabin and rear, and the shortest of the three is the bonnet at about a fifth of the length; 0.15 is under that with margin and above the single station a wing mirror or an aerial can own.
silhouettes.$minRoofSpan: 0.30 — P90 MINUS P10 OF THE STATION HEIGHTS, IN UNITS OF THE SUBJECT'S OWN HEIGHT, AND THE FLOOR IS DERIVED FROM THE REFERENCE RATHER THAN FROM WHAT THE FLEET DELIVERS. A rectangular prism reads exactly 0.000: every station of a prism reaches the same fraction of its own height, from any distance and any heading, which is what makes this fail on a box by construction. THE REFERENCE-ERA ARITHMETIC, three body kinds, each as (roof - shoulder) / roof: a three-box saloon at (1.42 - 0.93) / 1.42 = 0.345; a panel van at (2.20 - 1.18) / 2.20 = 0.464; a pickup at (1.80 - 1.13) / 1.80 = 0.372. The shallowest of the three is 0.345. THE MARGIN TAKEN OFF IT: the reading is a fraction of a segment walked one pixel at a time, and at 60 m a 1.42 m subject is 36.55 px, so one step is 0.027 of the height and a P90 - P10 difference can lose two of them, 0.055. 0.345 - 0.055 = 0.290, rounded to 0.30. PERCENTILES AND NOT MAX MINUS MIN, so one station that caught a wing mirror or the antialiased edge of a neighbour cannot be the whole finding.
silhouettes.$UNION_DEFECT: THE ROOFLINE READ FLAT AT THREE-QUARTER VIEW ON GEOMETRY THAT WAS NOT, AND THE CONTROL ABOVE COULD NOT SEE IT. Recorded beside `$DISCARDED_darkFraction` because it is the same failure one level down: not a statistic whose two answers were the same answer, but a MASK whose two answers were. The gate builds a subject`s mask as the union of its per-box convex hulls with no depth test between its own parts, and read the topmost pixel of that union above each station. A box of length l and width w seen at theta from broadside projects an image-horizontal span of l*cos(theta) + w*sin(theta), which GROWS as the subject turns away from broadside, while the sampled long axis projects L*(1-2*trim)*cos(theta), which SHRINKS. Past about 0.86 of the second by the first, a tall box`s hull covers every station and the roofline reads that one box at all of them. MEASURED THROUGH THE WHOLE RENDER PATH by tools/hullprobe.mjs, which places the control shapes as real 3D boxes in the live scene at the gate`s own camera pose: the three-box POSITIVE control scored 0.3187 / 0.3180 / 0.1723 / 0.0212 at 0 / 25 / 30 / 39 degrees against this block`s 0.30 floor, and the delivered wedge went 0.208 at broadside to 0.015 by 20 degrees. At 39 degrees a prism, a reference-era saloon and the delivered wedge ALL returned about 0.02. THE ATTRIBUTION IS THE WIDTH: the same three-box shape at 0.02 m wide — no lateral hull span, everything else identical — held 0.344 to 0.349 at every angle out to 65. A DEPTH-ORDERED MASK CANNOT REPAIR THIS, which is worth writing down because it is the obvious repair: the reading is SET MEMBERSHIP in a union, and ordering the pixels by depth gives each an owner and changes the set by nothing. Nor is there a spurious pixel to remove — the projected outline of a convex box IS the hull of its projected vertices. What was wrong was attributing a pixel above station a to station a. THE FIX is that the harness reports each box`s own extent along the subject`s long axis (`profile.boxAlong`) and the position of each station on it (`profile.stationAlong`), and a station is read against the boxes that SPAN it. IT MOVES READINGS IN THE LENIENT DIRECTION — the wedge from 0.021 to 0.208 — which is what CONTRACT §0 rule 5 exists to be suspicious of, so: NO THRESHOLD MOVED, and the guard is `shapeControlViews` below.
silhouettes.$shapeControlViews: A SHAPE CONTROL IS RUN OVER THE RANGE OF VIEWS THE POPULATION ACTUALLY CONTAINS, NOT AT ONE VIEW. This is what `$UNION_DEFECT` cost and it is the rule that comes out of it. The old control was a single orthographic side elevation and BOTH ITS DIRECTIONS HELD — prism 0.0000, three-box 0.3403 — while the delivered metric returned the same 0.02 for both shapes at three-quarter view. A control at one view can only certify one view. THE ANGLES: 0 to 70 degrees from broadside in the sweep below, which brackets what `highway_speed` delivers; beyond about 75 the axis projects under `minStationPx` and the subject is excluded on geometry before any pixel is read, so certifying there would be certifying nothing. THE DISTANCES: 15 m and 45 m, inside `maxDistanceM` at both ends, because the near-side top edge of a wide box projects higher above the mid-plane the closer it is (see `$overshoot`) and the control has to hold at both. THE WIDTH: 1.80 m, a reference-era saloon across the mirrors-off body, and it is the axis the defect lived on — at 0.02 m the old reading passed everywhere. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE REQUIRED AT EVERY VIEW: the prism under the floor and the three-box over it, at each of the angle-by-distance pairs. One view failing either direction fails the gate.
silhouettes.$minViewsTested: 12 OF THE 16 VIEWS, AND IT IS WHAT STOPS `DECLINED` BECOMING THE ANSWER EVERYWHERE. A view where the trimmed long axis projects under `minStationPx` x `stations` = 48 px is EXCLUDED BY THE INSTRUMENT before a pixel is read, which is the instrument working: at 45 m the 3.92 m trimmed axis foreshortens to 3.92*cos(theta), one pixel subtends 8.019e-4 rad, and 48 px needs cos(theta) >= 0.4419, i.e. theta <= 63.8 degrees — so 70 degrees at 45 m declines and 70 at 15 m does not. That exclusion has to stay exercisable or the sweep would never test it, so a view where BOTH controls decline is recorded and skipped rather than failed. THE FLOOR: all eight angles are admissible at 15 m and seven of eight at 45 m, so 15 are expected; 12 is under that and above the eight a single distance would give, so losing a whole distance fails. A view where ONE control declines and the other does not is always a failure — the two shapes are the same 4.90 m long seen from the same place, so they are admissible together or not at all.
silhouettes.$WIDTH: THE WIDTH ALONG THE LONG AXIS, CONTRACT §7.5, AND IT IS WRITTEN BEFORE THE GEOMETRY IT ASKS FOR EXISTS — the fourth assertion in this block added under that rule and the fourth confirmed RED first. WHY IT IS NOT A FOURTH PROPERTY BOLTED TO A BOX. Sessions 5, 6 and 6b added ground contact, colour and a stepped roofline to a body built from axis-aligned rectangular prisms. Every one of those assertions is green and the vehicles still read as boxes, because a stack of prisms has CONSTANT WIDTH BY DEFINITION: every corner is 90 degrees, every face is planar, nothing tapers and nothing is chamfered. Measured on the delivered wedge, every painted box is 1.86 to 1.92 m wide over a 4.90 m body — a 0.03 spread in units of its own width, and the roofline cannot see it because the roofline reads HEIGHT. THE READING: at the same `stations` the roofline uses, the harness returns a segment ACROSS the subject at `latHeight` of its own height reaching `latOvershoot` times its own half-width either side of its lateral mid-plane, and the gate reports the covered fraction of that segment as a multiple of the subject's own maximum width. A body of constant width reads THE SAME NUMBER AT EVERY STATION, so `widthSpan` is exactly 0.0000 for one — the assertion fails on a prism by construction rather than by calibration, which is the property `$DISCARDED_darkFraction` did not have.
silhouettes.$widthSpan_isNotWidthRoughness: TWO DIFFERENT ASSERTIONS WITH SIMILAR NAMES, AND THE PAIR IS WORTH DISAMBIGUATING BEFORE SOMEBODY CONFLATES THEM (CONTRACT §9 is a whole section about exactly that). `minWidthRoughness` is the PEDESTRIAN assertion: total variation of the mask's ROW WIDTHS down the image, i.e. how the outline narrows and widens with HEIGHT — a head over shoulders over two legs. `minWidthSpan` is the VEHICLE assertion: P90 minus P10 of the body's own width at stations ALONG ITS LONG AXIS — a nose narrower than the doors. Different axis, different kind, different statistic. Neither is a generalisation of the other and neither may be deleted in favour of the other.
silhouettes.$widthOverRead: THE ONE THING THAT CAN MAKE THIS METRIC LIE, DERIVED, BECAUSE TWO OF ITS FOUR EXCLUSIONS EXIST FOR IT. There is no depth test between a subject's own parts, so a probe point OUTSIDE the true width can still be covered by another point of the SAME box. Camera at the origin looking down -Z, the long axis at theta from broadside, the probe dh below the eye at depth d: a box point at (along a', lateral l', height offset v) lands on the probe point at lateral l exactly when l' = l + (v/dh)*(d*cos(theta) - l) and a' = a + (l - l')*tan(theta). THE HEIGHT TRADE IS FREE — covering a point 0.30 m outside the width at 25 m needs v = 1.1*0.30*cos(theta)/25 = 0.011 m, one centimetre, against boxes at least 0.20 m tall — so there is no bounding this by height. THE ALONG TRADE IS BOUNDED BY THE BOX'S OWN LENGTH, because a' must stay inside the box: at most (boxEnd - a)*cot(theta) on the plus side and (a - boxStart)*cot(theta) on the minus side, so THE TOTAL OVER-READ IS boxLength*cot(theta) WHATEVER THE STATION. That is why the metric works: a constant additive inflation cancels out of a difference of percentiles, so a body whose parts are all the same length reads (trueWidth_i + boxLength*cot(theta))/maxWidth and the SPAN of that is the span of the true widths, exactly. WHAT DOES NOT CANCEL is a spread in part lengths — see `$maxWidthBias`. AND IT MAKES THIS A NEAR-END-ON READING WHERE THE ROOFLINE IS A BROADSIDE ONE: cot(theta) vanishes end-on, which is precisely where the roofline's own long axis projects under `minStationPx` and it declines. The two populations are close to complementary. That is a finding rather than a convenience and it is why each carries its own `minMeasured`.
silhouettes.$latOvershoot: 1.60, AND IT IS `overshoot` ONE AXIS OVER PLUS ONE MORE JOB. Same job: the probe has to reach past the geometry or every station clips to 1.000 and a tapered body reports a prism's span. The extra job: it has to contain the `$widthOverRead` inflation, and where it does not the station SATURATES and is declined — which is the exclusion that keeps low angles out for a body whose parts are uniform, where the bias spread is zero and would otherwise admit everything. THE ARITHMETIC: the positive control's segments are 4.90/14 = 0.35 m, so its over-read is 0.35*cot(theta) and it fits inside 0.60 of a 1.80 m body's width — the margin 1.60 buys — while 0.35*cot(theta) <= 0.60*1.80, i.e. theta >= 17.9 degrees. Below that both controls saturate and the sweep records the view as declined. LARGER WOULD ADMIT SHALLOWER ANGLES AND COST RESOLUTION: the reading's quantisation is latOvershoot/steps of the subject's own width, so every increase here is paid for in `$minWidthSpan`'s margin.
silhouettes.$latHeight: 0.50 OF THE SUBJECT'S OWN HEIGHT, WHICH IS THE CENTRE OF `bodyBand`. That band is already established by `$bodyBand` as the body side on every one of the five types and as containing no glazing on any of them, so the probe measures the plan width of the BODY SIDE and not of a glasshouse or a sill. IT ALSO HAS TO CLEAR THE WHEELS AND SIT INSIDE THE LOWEST LONGITUDINAL SEGMENT, and 0.50 does on four of five types: wheel tops as a fraction of each type's own height are wedge 0.437, pod 0.312, van 0.296, hauler 0.258, moto 0.407, all under 0.50; the lowest segment top is wedge 0.577, pod 0.548, van 0.536, moto 0.815, all over 0.50. THE HAULER WAS THE EXCEPTION UNTIL SESSION 8 AND THE HISTORY IS KEPT BECAUSE IT EXPLAINS THE FLOOR'S POPULATION ARITHMETIC: its 7c bonnet reached 1.75 m of a 3.80 m body, 0.461, so the bonnet stations had no straddling box and were dropped — a 9.20 m tractor unit whose cab is half the height of its trailer genuinely was not one profile at mid-height. The session-8 hauler is one monolithic wedge (nose 1.86 m of a 3.62 m body, 0.514, above the probe) and all twelve of its stations read.
silhouettes.$minLatSegPx: 54 PIXELS OF PROJECTED PROBE, AND IT IS THE FOURTH INDEPENDENT ARRIVAL OF THE SAME 4 px. §5.12's `motionVectors.minExtentPx` derived 4 px from the TAA 3x3 neighbourhood clamp under half-pixel jitter; `$maxDistanceM` derived 60 m from the 0.16 m ground gap spanning 4 px; `$minStationPx` derived 4 px from telling two stations apart. THIS ONE: the shallowest width difference the assertion rests on is the floor itself, `minWidthSpan` = 0.12 of the subject's own width, which is 0.12/1.60 = 0.075 of the probe's own length, and for 0.075 of the probe to span at least 4 px the probe must project to at least 4/0.075 = 53.3 px. Rounded UP to 54. WHAT IT EXCLUDES IS BROADSIDE: at theta = 0 the lateral axis points straight down the line of sight and projects to nothing, so a width read there is a measurement of the resampler — the exact mirror of `minStationPx` excluding an end-on roofline. At `maxDistanceM` = 60 m a 1.94 m wedge's probe is 1247*3.104*sin(theta)/60 = 64.5*sin(theta) px, so 60 m admits theta >= 56.8 degrees; at 25 m it admits theta >= 21 degrees.
silhouettes.$maxWidthBias: 0.03 OF THE SUBJECT'S OWN WIDTH, AND IT IS THE BOUND ON THE TWO PARTS OF `$widthOverRead` THAT DO NOT CANCEL. TERM ONE, MEASURED: the over-read is boxLength*cot(theta), so it is common to every station only while every station's widest spanning box is the same length. A bonnet of 1.85 m beside a rear deck of 1.45 m inflates their two stations by different amounts, and the difference is (1.85 - 1.45)*cot(theta)/width — at 45 degrees that is 0.40/1.80 = 0.222 on a body of constant width, against a 0.12 floor. The gate measures that spread per subject from the delivered `boxAlong` and the projected foreshortening. TERM TWO, DERIVED, AND THE §7.3.1 SWEEP IS WHAT FOUND IT: solving the covering condition exactly rather than to first order leaves `-boxLength*cot(theta)*a/(d*sin(theta))`, which is LINEAR IN THE STATION POSITION, so a common over-read still drifts along the length. See `measureWidthProfile` for the derivation and for the four predicted-against-measured pairs it was checked with. THE TWO ARE ADDED and the subject is declined above 0.03. IT IS A DECLINE AND NOT A SUBTRACTION, deliberately: subtracting a computed bias from a measured reading would make the reading partly a calculation, and a calculation that over-corrected would MANUFACTURE a span — the lenient direction, on a metric whose whole job is to refuse one.
silhouettes.$maxWidthBias_isLoadBearing: IT IS NOT A TIDINESS EXCLUSION AND HERE IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS SO. With the exclusion switched off (`maxWidthBias` 99) and everything else identical, the CONSTANT-WIDTH controls read, over the 24 views of `widthControlViews`: `segPrism` up to 0.1502 at 25 degrees / 15 m, `longPrism` up to 0.1202 at 85 degrees / 30 m, `stepPrism` up to 0.0979 at 75 degrees / 15 m. TWO OF THOSE CLEAR THE 0.12 FLOOR — a body of exactly constant width would have passed an assertion about taper at 2 of 24 views, which is `$DISCARDED_darkFraction`'s defect in a metric that otherwise works. With the exclusion on at 0.03 the worst constant-width reading at ANY admitted view is 0.0197 (`segPrism`, 55 degrees / 30 m), which is 6.1x under the floor, and the positive control's worst is 0.1424, which is 1.19x over it. 0.03 was chosen as the largest tolerance at which no constant-width arm reads above 0.021 anywhere, and it is 4.0x under the floor it protects.
silhouettes.$minWidthSpan: 0.12 — P90 MINUS P10 OF THE STATION WIDTHS, IN UNITS OF THE SUBJECT'S OWN MAXIMUM WIDTH, DERIVED FROM A REFERENCE RATHER THAN FROM WHAT THE FLEET DELIVERS. A body of constant width reads exactly 0.0000. THE REFERENCE, and it is run through this instrument's own sampling rather than estimated: a 4.90 m x 1.80 m three-box saloon's plan half-width at door-handle height, holding full width from the front wheel arch to the rear one and narrowing into a radiused bumper corner at each end, is `WIDTH_TAPER` in tools/lib/silhouette.mjs. Sampled at 12 stations over the trimmed 3.92 m with 3 sub-samples medianed, its readings are 0.84 0.91 0.96 0.99 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 0.98 0.94 0.88 0.80, whose P10 is 0.844 and P90 is 1.000, SO THE REFERENCE SPAN IS 0.156. THE MARGINS TAKEN OFF IT: 0.013 for the walk, which is one step at each end of a 256-step parameter walk at latOvershoot/steps = 0.00625 of the body's own width; and 0.023 for the population, being a body at 45 m whose probe is 65 px with its own antialiased hull edge, read as a median of three sub-samples over a 0.33 m band rather than as a point. 0.156 - 0.013 - 0.023 = 0.120. WHAT THE CONTROL THEN MEASURED THROUGH THE WHOLE SAMPLING PATH, both numbers printed because a derivation that turned out conservative is worth more than one quietly replaced (§9 rule 4): the same reference shape scores 0.1334 to 0.1563 across the 11 admissible views of `widthControlViews`, so the 0.036 of margin taken off covers an observed loss of 0.023 and the floor clears the reference's WORST view by 1.19x. IT IS ALSO 4.0x THE 0.03 `maxWidthBias` PERMITS and 6.1x the 0.0197 a constant-width body actually reads at its worst admitted view — the same kind of statement `$minGroundContrast_measured` makes about a slab, and the ratio that matters more than the derivation.
silhouettes.$minWidthSpan_notAllVehiclesTaper: WHAT THIS FLOOR IS A STATEMENT ABOUT, SAID PLAINLY, BECAUSE `$minRoofSpan` COULD DERIVE FROM THE SHALLOWEST OF THREE REFERENCE TYPES AND THIS ONE CANNOT. A real panel van is very nearly a box in plan: sampled the same way, a 5.60 m x 2.10 m van whose only narrowing is the nose into its bumper reads 0.86 0.94 0.99 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00 1.00, whose span is 0.055 — well under this floor, and a floor derived from it would be 0.04 or less, which is the bias bound and therefore no floor at all. SO THE FLOOR IS DERIVED FROM THE SALOON AND IT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THIS FLEET'S DESIGN LANGUAGE RATHER THAN ABOUT ALL ROAD VEHICLES: every body in this world tapers in plan by at least 0.12 of its own width, including the van and including the tractor unit, which a 1995 panel van would not. That is a content decision and it is the one CONTRACT §7.5 asks for. `minPassFraction` is 0.75, so one type of five may be shallower than the floor; it is NOT room for the van and the hauler both, which together are 30% of the fleet by weight.
silhouettes.$widthControlViews: A SHAPE CONTROL IS RUN OVER THE RANGE OF VIEWS THE POPULATION CONTAINS (CONTRACT §7.3.1) AND THIS SWEEP IS NOT `shapeControlViews`, BECAUSE THE TWO METRICS ARE ADMISSIBLE AT OPPOSITE ENDS OF THE SAME RANGE. The roofline sweeps 0 to 70 degrees from broadside and declines past about 64 at 45 m where the trimmed long axis projects under 48 px. The width declines at the BOTTOM of that range — 0 degrees puts the lateral axis down the line of sight — and is at its most exact end-on, so it sweeps 15 to 85. THE ANGLES: 15 exercises the saturation decline at 15 m (17.9 degrees is where the positive control's over-read stops fitting inside `latOvershoot`) and the pixel decline at 45 m; 85 is where cot(theta) is 0.0875 and the reading is essentially exact. THE DISTANCES: 15 m and 45 m, the same pair as the roofline sweep and inside `maxDistanceM` at both ends, because the probe's projected length scales as 1/distance and `minLatSegPx` therefore bites at a different angle at each. THE WIDTH: 1.80 m, the same reference-era body across the mirrors-off body. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE REQUIRED AT EVERY ADMISSIBLE VIEW: `segPrism` under the floor and `taper` over it. The two are the SAME 14 segments of the SAME length at the SAME maximum width differing only in the width profile, which is what makes the comparison an attribution rather than a demonstration — a one-box prism against a fourteen-segment loft differs in part length as well as in taper, and `$widthOverRead` says the metric responds to both.
silhouettes.$minWidthViewsTested: 9 OF THE 24 VIEWS, AND THE LOW FRACTION IS THE INSTRUMENT'S ADMISSIBLE RANGE RATHER THAN A SWEEP THAT HAS GONE QUIET. Three exclusions each bite from a different side and all three are exercised: the probe projects under `minLatSegPx` (15 and 25 degrees at 30 and 45 m), the reading saturates `latOvershoot` (15 degrees at 15 m), and `maxWidthBias` declines the rest of the shallow angles. MEASURED, over the 8 angles x 3 distances: 11 views admissible — 2 at 15 m, 4 at 30 m, 5 at 45 m. The floor is 9, which is under 11 and above the 5 a single distance would give, so losing a whole distance fails; and each distance is separately required to contribute at least one, for the same reason the roofline sweep requires it. A view where BOTH controls decline is recorded and skipped; a view where ONE declines and the other does not is always a failure, because the two shapes are the same length and the same maximum width seen from the same place and are admissible together or not at all. MEASURED: zero mismatches across all 24 views and across six tolerances from 0.015 to 0.05.
silhouettes.$widthControlDistances: THREE DISTANCES RATHER THAN THE ROOFLINE SWEEP'S TWO, because this metric has an exclusion that scales as 1/distance and one that scales as distance, so the admissible angle band MOVES with distance and a middle distance is what shows the band rather than its two ends. `minLatSegPx` admits shallower angles the NEARER the subject (the probe subtends more); the `maxWidthBias` perspective term admits shallower angles the FURTHER away it is (the drift is over-read times alongSpan over depth). At 15 m the band is 75-85 degrees, at 30 m it is 55-85 and at 45 m it is 45-85 — the two bounds cross over between them, which is the behaviour a two-distance sweep would have shown as two disconnected results.
silhouettes.$widthRedBeforeBuilding: CONFIRMED RED AGAINST THE CURRENT BODIES BEFORE A LINE OF GEOMETRY WAS CHANGED, WHICH IS §7.2's LAST REQUIREMENT AND THE ONE THAT CAUGHT `darkFraction`. RED TWICE, FROM TWO INDEPENDENT DIRECTIONS, and the pair is the point (§9 rule 2). (1) IN THE GATE, off the delivered frame: `perfcheck --route=highway_speed --runs=1` measured 16 vehicles, of which ZERO could be read for width and NINE were declined because their own parts are too long along the axis for the over-read to cancel. So the assertion lands on `minWidthMeasured` as UNRUN rather than on the span. (2) FROM THE DELIVERED GEOMETRY, `tools/hullprobe.mjs`'s `fromBoxes` column, which reads `traffic._internal.BODY_TYPES` off the live module and applies the same 12 stations, the same 3 medianed sub-samples and the same straddle rule to each box's own `wide`: wedge 0.0309, pod 0.0349, van 0.0673, hauler 0.0152, moto 0.1111. ALL FIVE TYPES ARE UNDER THE 0.12 FLOOR, the median of the five is 0.0349, and the wedge — a third of the fleet by weight — is 3.9x under it. THE TWO REDS SAY DIFFERENT THINGS AND BOTH ARE NEEDED: the first says the fleet is unmeasurable, which on its own proves nothing about the fleet; the second says what the fleet IS, and it is a body of constant width to within 3% over four of its five types. THE SAME COLUMN VALIDATES THE INSTRUMENT IN THE OTHER DIRECTION: the positive control's geometry implies 0.1560 and the projection measured 0.1515 at 85 degrees — the derivation in `$minWidthSpan` predicted 0.156 by hand and the geometry path returned 0.1560, so the sampling chain agrees with itself to four decimals.
silhouettes.$fovYDrift: A NUMBER THAT IS RIGHT ABOUT ONE QUANTITY AND USED FOR ANOTHER, FOUND WHILE FIXING THE ABOVE AND NOT FIXED HERE. `$maxDistanceM` derives 60 m from one pixel subtending 2*tan(25 deg)/1440 = 6.4765e-4 rad, which is the 50-degree vertical field the camera is CONSTRUCTED with in main.js. `camera.js` gives the `highway_speed` route `fov: 60`, and that is the field the measured frames are taken through. At 60 degrees one pixel is 2*tan(30 deg)/1440 = 8.019e-4 rad, so the 0.16 m ground gap spans 4 px at 0.16 / (4 * 8.019e-4) = 49.9 m rather than 61.76 m, and `maxDistanceM: 60` admits vehicles whose ground gap is 3.3 px. The direction is LAX for the population and CONSERVATIVE for the assertion it was derived for — an under-resolved gap blurs toward the road and lowers the contrast, which makes `minGroundContrast` harder rather than easier — so it is recorded rather than changed in the same session as a geometry rebuild. `$levelTolerance` and `$minRoofSpan` carry the same 6.4765e-4: recomputed at 60 degrees the tolerance would be 0.136 rather than 0.10 and the span margin 0.068 rather than 0.055, i.e. the delivered floor of 0.30 is STRICTER than its own derivation, which is why it does not move.
silhouettes.$roofLevels_notAsserted: THE LEVEL COUNT IS REPORTED AND NOT ASSERTED, and the reason is a false negative that would have punished the exact geometry this block asks for. `roofLevels` is single-linkage over the station heights at `levelTolerance`, and single linkage CHAINS: a roofline that ramps continuously from a low nose to a high cabin — which is the raked front CONTRACT §7.3 asks for in the same paragraph — collapses into one cluster and would score 1. An assertion that fails a body for having the property it exists to reward is the `$DISCARDED_darkFraction` mistake pointing the other way, so the count is printed beside the span (§9 rule 2) and the span carries the verdict.
silhouettes.$profileRangeFloor: 0.08. Both roughness figures divide by the profile's range, and a profile that is flat to within noise would divide by nearly nothing and report a large number from rounding. The divisor is floored at 8% of the subject's own body luminance (or its own maximum width), so a genuinely flat profile scores at most TV/0.08 - 1 over a TV that is itself noise, and in practice 0. Chosen as half the smallest step the metric is supposed to see: the shallowest real feature is a glazing band at 0.25 against a body at 0.60, which is a step of 0.35 in units where the body is 0.60, i.e. 0.58 of it.
silhouettes.$minVisibleFraction: 0.55, AND IT APPLIES TO EVERY BAND THE SUBJECT IS JUDGED ON AND NOT ONLY TO THE SUBJECT. A subject whose nearer neighbours cover more than 45% of it is measured on a sliver, and a sliver's row profile is the profile of whatever part happened to survive. Occluding subjects are SUBTRACTED rather than causing the subject to be dropped — the first version dropped any subject a nearer one overlapped at all, which on a street where vehicles queue left 2 measurable out of 14 — but a subtraction that removes most of the body is not a measurement of the body. THE BAND-LEVEL CHECK WAS ADDED AFTER LOOKING AT A FAILURE, and it is the one number in this block that came out of a picture rather than out of arithmetic: a hauler 31 m away with a crowd of pedestrians in front of it was 82% visible OVERALL and had its ground band 85% hidden, so the 948 pixels that survived in that band were the PAVEMENT SEEN BETWEEN PEOPLE'S LEGS and it scored a ground contrast of -0.561 with the darkest wheels in the frame directly behind them. The band-visibility check EXCLUDES such a subject from the population; it is computed from masks alone and never touches a luminance, so it cannot degenerate into dropping the subjects that fail, and `minMeasured` is what stops it excluding everything.
silhouettes.$minRowSamples: 6 pixels in a row before that row contributes a median, and 6 in a band before the band is measured. Below that the median is one or two antialiased edge pixels blended with the road.
silhouettes.$minPassFraction: 0.75 of the measured population must clear each floor, and the MEDIAN must clear it too. Two statements rather than one because they fail differently: a median that clears while a third of the fleet does not is a fleet with a broken minority, and a pass fraction that clears while the median does not is arithmetically impossible, so the pair pins the distribution from both ends. NOT the minimum, and the reason is written in tools/lib/silhouette.mjs: there is no depth buffer here, so a vehicle behind a lamp post is measured through the lamp post, and a gate whose verdict is one contaminated subject is a gate that goes red for the wrong reason.
silhouettes.$chromaEpsilon: 0.02 in (r/(r+g+b), b/(r+g+b)) chromaticity. A neutral grey sits at (0.3333, 0.3333); a paint read at (0.3533, 0.3333) is 6% more red than green within its own sum, which is about where a person picks two cars apart in a queue. Single linkage, so the count is the number of connected components and a palette smeared evenly along one axis does not score as many clusters as its endpoints suggest.
silhouettes.$minChromaClusters: 4, WHICH IS `trafficLights.minBodyTypes` DELIBERATELY. The rule this block exists to satisfy says a floor that counts categories must be paired with one measuring the property the categories are assumed to carry; a paired floor at a different number would be two claims rather than one claim checked twice. CHROMATICITY AND NOT COLOUR: two vehicles differ in delivered luminance either because their paint differs or because one is in shade, so a cluster count that used luminance would pass a fleet of identical grey boxes parked half in sunlight — which is the exact frame that prompted this. Chromaticity is invariant to the sun going behind a building and is not invariant to the paint.
silhouettes.$requirePaletteAgreement: THE SAME QUANTITY DERIVED TWO WAYS AND PRINTED BOTH WAYS, CONTRACT §9 rule 2. `harness.instanceColourPalette()` reports how many distinct body colours were WRITTEN into the live `instanceColor` buffer; the cluster count above reports how many ARRIVED in the frame. If the first is six and the second is one, the attribute is not reaching `diffuseColor` and adding palette entries will not change a pixel. This project has already been within one conclusion of getting that wrong: three defines USE_COLOR in the VERTEX prefix from `vertexColors` alone and in the FRAGMENT prefix from `vertexColors || instancingColor || batchingColor`, and reading one of the two prefixes and concluding is the whole mistake. The assertion is that the written palette is at least as large as the floor — a palette smaller than the floor is a content bug, and a palette that clears it while the frame does not is a plumbing bug, and the two failure messages say which.
silhouettes.$kinds: WHICH CLAIM APPLIES TO WHICH KIND, AND THE ABSENCES ARE THE POINT. A vehicle gets a ground-contact claim, a tone-profile claim and a colour claim; a pedestrian gets a width-profile claim and a colour claim and NO ground-contact claim, because a person has no ground clearance and asserting one would be asserting something nobody said. A threshold that is absent is skipped rather than defaulted, so a kind is never failed on a claim its budget never made. `minMeasured` is higher for pedestrians because there are 360 of them against 160 vehicles and they stand on both pavements.
silhouettes.$pedestrianChroma: 3, NOT 4. The pedestrian claim is clothing rather than paint, and city-budget.json already fixes the chromatic garment fraction at one in five with four garment chromaticities, all of them drawn from city.js SIGN_CHROMA. Four measured clusters would require every one of the four to be in frame at once out of a sample of a dozen, which is a claim about sampling and not about content. Three is what a crowd delivers when the garments exist at all, and 1 is what it delivers when they do not.

vehicle.$minProfileMeasured: 5, AND IT IS A SMALLER FLOOR THAN `minMeasured` FOR A REASON THAT IS ABOUT THE ROUTE. A vehicle seen end-on is measurable for the ground gap and the tone profile and is NOT measurable for the roofline, so the profile population is a subset of the measured one and asserting one count for both would let a route on which nothing is ever seen broadside satisfy the roofline floor with an empty set. THE ARITHMETIC WHEN 5 WAS WRITTEN: `minMeasured` is 6 over three pooled poses; the excluded case is the vehicle within about 11 degrees of straight ahead, which on `highway_speed` is the one in the camera's own lane out of the carriageway's three, so at most a third goes — 6 x 2/3 = 4, rounded up to 5. WHAT WAS THEN MEASURED, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE ARITHMETIC PREDICTED: 9 of 18 measured vehicles carried a readable roofline, which is a HALF rather than two thirds, and the smallest surviving axis was 71.6 px against the 48 px bound. The prediction was wrong because it counted only the heading and the population also loses the small and the distant — a 3.4 m pod at 40 m projects 82.8 px of axis and a 4.9 m wedge at 31.7 m projects 149.5 px, so the bound bites on length as much as on angle. The floor is NOT moved: 5 was written before the measurement and 9 clears it. Both numbers are here because a derivation that turned out wrong is worth more than a derivation that was quietly replaced (CONTRACT §9 rule 4).
vehicle.$minWidthMeasured: 5, THE SAME FLOOR AS `minProfileMeasured` AND A THIRD POPULATION. §7.5's reading is admissible where the roofline's is not and vice versa — `$widthOverRead` — so one count cannot serve both and asserting the roofline's would let a route on which nothing is ever seen end-on satisfy the width floor with an empty set.
